original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove the all-modulus two-short-row annihilator obstruction for balanced depth-four chain connectors, and give an exact 4m construction with two short rows at m=8t, c=4t for every t>=1.
scope_change_reason: The alphabet remains unsigned and complete. This extends the open row-complexity question of PR4280 rather than adding a connector operation; it distinguishes unit coefficients from composite-characteristic exceptions.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result: it prunes row-model searches for unit coefficients in composite characteristic and supplies a minimal-call infinite subfamily for nonunit coefficients. No physical supplier saving is inferred.
stop_rule: Stop after the first verified original extension of the row obstruction and a sharp composite family. Leave classification and general unit constructions open.
evidence: Written all-modulus proofs in README.md; standalone exact checks of 64 new family words, chronological counts, UT5 matrices, 128 dirty-register replays, a bounded annihilator relaxation and rejection controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which nonzero coefficients admit a balanced depth-four connector with exactly two short rows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The annihilator condition is necessary but does not enforce the monotone profile budgets; a classification would identify when a two-row search is justified.
open_questions.first_step: Fix m, the pair L and m-L, and enumerate the admissible beta and rho profiles subject to the five vanishing congruences.
open_questions.blocked_by: The new necessary condition is not claimed sufficient.

open_questions.question: Can three short rows realize every unit coefficient for every m>=6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The obstruction proves three are necessary for units in all characteristics; an upper construction would close that row-complexity gap.
open_questions.first_step: Use the three-short-row instances in PR4280 as design examples and seek a parametric family satisfying the profile budgets.
open_questions.blocked_by: A uniform construction for unit coefficients remains unknown here.

coordination.scope: Live open PRs, own recent PRs, latest handoff comments, cached complete remote overlap, and targeted main/merged searches; sparse local note coverage is incomplete.
